On 26 October 2023, Israeli warplanes conducted two airstrikes over the forests of Labbouneh (Tyr), likely resulting in the death of a Hezbollah fighter who was announced dead an hour after the strike. International organizations have accused Israel of using white phosphorous bombs during the current war between Hezbollah and Israel.

On 21 March 2025, either Russian or Ukrainian forces blew up or shelled with artillery the building of the 'Sudzha' gas measuring station that is located next to the border checkpoint near Oleshnya (Sudzhanskiy, Kursk). Casualties unknown. The station was severely damaged. Both sides accused each other: Russia accused Ukraine of blowing the station up and breaking the verbal agreement between the two sides to cease fire on objects of energy infrastructure, Ukraine accused Russian of shelling the station with the goal of blaming Ukraine for breaking the agreement. The station is part of the gas pipeline that until January 2025 was used to transfer gas internationally to Europe through Ukraine.

On 18 August 2024, Ukrainian Directorate of Intelligence launched kamikaze drones at an oil depot in Proletarsk (Proletarskiy, Rostov). Russian military intercepted a few drones, the debris that fell on the 'Kavkaz' oil depot warehouse premises caused diesel fuel to catch fire. When the firefighters attempted to extinguish the fire they were attacked by drones once again. The fire continued to burn for 16 days (before it was extinguished) on a territory of 10 square km, and according to some sources, led to a serious deterioration in air quality in the city. 49 firefighters were injured in the result of fire, subsequent explosions and during the fire extinguishing process. 30 fuel tanks, each of which can contain up to 500 square meters of fuel were destroyed or damaged.
